# A cup of tea on a Thursday

The bourbon biscuits always go first. We’ve taken to hiding a packet for the later group, which seems only fair.

I help with the tea trolley in the day therapy unit at Wensum Vale Hospice on Thursday afternoons. There are four of us on a rota meant for six, so we could do with two more. One of our volunteers moved to Sheffield over the summer to be near her grandchildren, and another had a knee operation. Both are much missed, though I imagine the biscuits have noticed less than we have.

I started in March 2022, about eighteen months after retiring. I’d spent 41 years in bookkeeping, mostly for a builders’ merchant in Dereham, and then found myself with no particular reason to go out most weeks. I drifted a bit. Having somewhere to be on a Thursday helped with that more than I expected.

The day unit usually sees around 14 to 18 patients on a Thursday. Some come for the art group, some for a hand massage, and some just for company. Most go home afterwards. It’s mostly a noisy, rather jolly place. There are sad days, of course, and some weeks are hard, but the staff look after us when that happens.

You don’t need any nursing skills to do the trolley. You do need to be able to push it, remember who takes what, and listen. It turns out that 41 years of keeping ledgers straight is quite useful when it comes to remembering the teas. Mr Hollis, a retired signalman, takes two sugars and tells me about the 1953 floods every week. The story changes a little each time. I’ve stopped correcting the dates.

It helps if you can laugh at yourself, too. In my first week I spilled an entire jug of milk over the trolley. A patient called Pat laughed so much she had to be given a tissue. She told me it was the best afternoon she’d had in a month. I’d like to say I planned it, but I was too busy mopping up.

The shift is **1.30 to 4pm on a Thursday**, and the commitment is **one Thursday a fortnight**. Bridget, our volunteer coordinator, does the induction, which takes about two hours. There’s also a short food hygiene course to do online, and the hospice pays for that.

If you’ve wondered about volunteering but thought you wouldn’t know enough, please don’t let that put you off. We all had a first week, and I hope yours involves less milk than mine.

There’s a **volunteer open afternoon on Tuesday 24 November at 2pm in the Willow Room**. There’ll be tea and biscuits, and no obligation. It would be lovely if at least two of you came along to see what you think. You can also ring Bridget on the volunteering line.
